items.answer: One surface mismatch: the requirement table writes the dropdown label as '≤3 days' (unicode) while C1 fixes the exact string '<=3 days'. Resolved by C1, which is explicit and confirmed by the business unit; '≤3 days' is therefore NOT accepted and throws RangeError (C5 exact matching). Also the labels '>60 days' and '>90 days' overlap numerically with '>3 days'; each option is a single selected value, so the mapping is by option string, not by number. No other contradictions.

items.answer: daysWithDelayWl(option: string) -> 0|2|3|4; delayCountWl(option: string) -> 0|1|2; DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = ['no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'] (in this order); DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS = ['0','1','>1'] (in this order). Returns plain numbers. Input trimmed (String.prototype.trim), exact case-sensitive match. Named exports in the two .mjs files.

Any value not in the option list after trimming (unknown string, different case, '', whitespace-only, '≤3 days') and any non-string (null, undefined, number, object) throws RangeError. Never returns a fallback/default WL.

No targets; O(1) lookup on a 3-5 element list.

Only input validation applies: strict exact-match whitelist, RangeError otherwise, no eval or dynamic lookup by arbitrary key (guard against inherited property names such as 'constructor' or '__proto__' if a lookup object is used: these must throw RangeError).
Inputs are dropdown labels, no personal data; nothing is logged.
No auditing in this slice.
Pure functions, no logging, metrics or tracing.
No regulation constrains this mapping beyond the POC's WL rules, which are already captured in the requirements.

Dev unit tests (TDD) in test/indicators/<name>.test.mjs per indicator via node:test + node:assert/strict; QA integration tests in test/integration/indicators/. Full verification: node --test. Cover every option, option list order, trim, case sensitivity, non-strings, empty string.

items.answer: 'Trimmed' means String.prototype.trim() (leading/trailing whitespace incl. tabs/newlines). e.g. '  >3 days ' -> 2. Internal whitespace is not altered ('>3  days' -> RangeError).

items.answer: Indicator 3 option '>1' means more than one delay in 12 months -> WL 2; '1' -> WL 1; '0' -> WL 0. Counting is the caller's job.
Indicator 2 only yields WL 0, 2, 3 or 4; WL 1 is never produced by this indicator (no option maps to 1). This is intended per the requirement.

The two devs touch disjoint files (daysWithDelay.mjs/delayCount.mjs and their tests); no shared module or index file is created, so no merge conflict is expected. An src/indicators/index.mjs barrel is not requested and must not be added.
